_comment: Emberreach settlement structures. Each entry: cost (level 1), cost_growth (multiplier per further level), production (per level per hour), max_level, unlocks (what system it opens), description and effect_note. All costs are paid from the settlement store, which fills from the structures themselves — the settlement is a self-contained economy that feeds the main game's bottlenecks.

township_building_lumber.name: Lumber Yard
township_building_lumber.description: Sawpits and drying racks. The yard is what lets the settlement pay its own timber bills without taking you off the frontier.
township_building_lumber.effect_note: Relieves the early timber bottleneck for construction and Kilncraft

township_building_farm.name: Terrace Farm
township_building_farm.description: Ash-heavy soil terraced into strips. Not good land, but it is land.
township_building_farm.effect_note: Food supports population and the trader's crates

township_building_homes.name: Homes
township_building_homes.description: Roofs, walls and a hearth. The settlement exists because people agreed to sleep here.
township_building_homes.effect_note: Population is the gate on every larger structure

township_building_mine.name: Quarry Adit
township_building_mine.description: A short adit into the ridge, shored with whatever the lumber yard could spare.
township_building_mine.effect_note: Stone unlocks larger construction; metal feeds the smelter

township_building_smelter.name: Smelter
township_building_smelter.description: A stone kiln that runs on settlement labour rather than your own attention.

township_building_workshop.name: Workshop
township_building_workshop.description: Benches, tools and a first honest attempt at quality control.
township_building_workshop.unlocks: +1% chance per level to keep Artifice materials
township_building_workshop.effect_note: Produces trade goods the trader exchanges for crates

township_building_apothecary.name: Apothecary
township_building_apothecary.description: Drying racks, a still and a locked cabinet. The marsh supplies the rest.
township_building_apothecary.unlocks: +2% chance per level to keep Apothecary herbs
township_building_apothecary.effect_note: Reagents reduce the herb bottleneck in Apothecary work

township_building_training_grounds.name: Training Grounds
township_building_training_grounds.description: A staked yard, practice arms and a board of everything that has gone wrong so far.
township_building_training_grounds.unlocks: +1% accuracy with every combat style per level
township_building_training_grounds.effect_note: Drills are traded for Huntsman coins; the grounds sharpen every style's aim

township_building_storehouse.name: Storehouse
township_building_storehouse.description: Dry, shelved and guarded. The frontier's real bottleneck is almost always space.

township_building_lodge.name: Expedition Lodge
township_building_lodge.description: Maps on the wall, packs on the floor. Everything a party needs before it leaves.
township_building_lodge.effect_note: Supplies are packed into combat draughts; the lodge stretches every meal

township_building_temple.name: Shrine
township_building_temple.description: The old rite, kept honestly. Every name accounted for, every debt settled.
township_building_temple.unlocks: Faith for the Observance; -2% Devotion point cost per level
township_building_temple.effect_note: Faith converts to prayer points, easing long Devotion sessions

township_building_school.name: Schoolhouse
township_building_school.description: Slate boards and a bell. Residents who know a trade teach it to anyone who will sit still.
township_building_school.effect_note: Pick one skill for the residents to study; it earns XP every hour, online or offline

township_building_observatory.name: Starreading Terrace
township_building_observatory.description: A flat plinth above the ash line, levelled for instruments the settlement cannot yet build.
township_building_observatory.effect_note: The trader sifts astral dust into Starreading dust, removing that grind bottleneck
